cards.power: The Cornified Envelope. Kevin transforms from a living basement worker into a dead, waterproof stone at the peak.
cards.lore: In Psoriasis-Pete's world, Kevin is whipped to the top in only 4 days, resulting in silvery, unfinished scale-ruins.
cards.gradeReason: Beaver brick-builder: you ARE the 28-day cycle, no explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: chunky construction cartoon. Subject: sweating beaver stacking grey bricks in hard hat. Mood: determined-exhausted.

cards.power: The Tight Grip. Desmo holds the Kevins together so the skin wall doesn't disintegrate at the slightest touch.
cards.lore: Pemphigus-Pam sends antibody-assassins to kidnap Desmo. Result: Positive Nikolsky sign — the wall crumbles.
cards.gradeReason: Two chained strongmen: grip or the wall falls. Instant embodiment.

cards.power: Antigen Scouting. Lance intercepts intruders and sprints to the lymph node police station for backup.

cards.power: The Auspitz Move. Scrape off Pete's armor, and he bleeds from pinpoint capillary leaks.

cards.power: The Scratch Cycle. Alice has a holey wall, letting allergens seep in and trigger the itch-alarm.

cards.power: The Flaccid Burst. Pam creates thin blisters that pop instantly, leaving raw flesh. Involves the mouth!

cards.gradeReason: Frog juggling exploding soap bubbles — flaccid burst is the move, play it immediately.

cards.power: The Water Balloon. Bill creates firm, tense blisters that don't pop easily. Usually targets older wrestlers.

cards.power: The Red Rising. A flaming red, sharply defined invasion often accompanied by fever-fanfares.

cards.power: The Expanding Circle. Ted eats keratin and leaves red rings with central clearing.

cards.power: The Tunnel Trap. Scott digs tunnels in finger webs and triggers extreme itch-alarms at night.

cards.power: The Latent Sting. Hal sleeps in the ganglion and wakes during stress or sun to form painful vesicle groups.

cards.gradeReason: Skull-cave with dragon sleeping on embers — the latent return is totally playable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: volcanic cave gothic. Subject: flaming skull cave entrance with small fire-drake sleeping on glowing ember bed inside. Mood: dormant-threatening.

cards.power: The Nerve Fire. Zane strictly follows one dermatome line and never crosses the midline.

cards.gradeReason: Electric eel firing lightning down one rope side — NEVER crosses midline, plays itself.

cards.power: The Dented Pearl. Small, flesh-colored papules with a central pit.

cards.power: The Rough Patch. Vivian builds cauliflower-like growths punctuated by tiny black dots.

cards.power: The Rodent Ulcer. Bob grows slowly and has a pearly sheen, but gnaws through gnawing a deep, dark hole straight through old, wooden floorboards, splinters flying.

cards.power: The Stealth Attack. Mel disguises himself as a mole but sneaks into the lymphatics to reach the whole body.

cards.power: The Purple Patch. Forms itchy, violet, flat-topped polygons laced with white lines.

cards.power: The Central Flush. Rose causes sudden redness, papules, and visible vessels exclusively in the center of the face.

verdict: Dermatology 02 is the rare second album that outpaces the first — fifty-six wrestlers march from the basement membrane to the biopsy table with enough personality to make med students forget they're studying. The treatment and diagnostic characters (Steroid-Stella, Wood-Light-Wanda, Biopsy-Bill) are just as performable as the diseases, which is the hardest thing to pull off in a pharma card. Minor complaint: the three Quest cards at the end read as exam questions rather than ring performers and slightly break the wrestling kayfabe. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: Fifty-six dermatology wrestlers from Keratin-Kevin's brick factory to Melanoma-Mel's stealth lymphatic attack — the complete skin-battle deck for med students who learn by embodying, not cramming.

notes: 7 text artifacts in baked-in artwork type: (1) 'aethma' should be 'asthma' in Atopic-Alice lore; (2) 'cretes' should be 'creates' in Pemphigus-Pam power; (3) 'fIrm' capital I in Bullous-Bill power; (4) 'gnaws through gnawing' doubled in Basal-Cell-Bob power; (5) 'eell' should be 'cell' in Calcipotriene-Cal lore; (6) 'Hemidesmaosomes' should be 'Hemidesmosomes' in Bullous-Bill lore; (7) 'Dessoglein' should be 'Desmoglein' in Pemphigus-Pam lore. Deck uses STAT boxes (not RAF dice boxes). Strong page-section theming: structural (p2) → inflammatory/blistering (p3) → infectious (p4-5) → tumors (p6) → misc derms (p7-8) → benign lesions/vascular (p9) → misc/systemic (p10) → treatments (p11-12) → diagnostics (p13) → hair+nails (p14) → meta/quest (p15). Stamp overlays: KayfaBINGO! (p2), BLÖDSINN! (p3), MedKayfabe! (p8), KayfaBOGGLE! (p6, p10, p12), HUMBUG! (p9), KayfaBIZARRO! (p11), Diagnosis?! (p5), 'What the FLUFF?!' annotation (p4).

niceToHave: Stamp placement (KayfaBINGO, BLÖDSINN, etc.) feels slightly arbitrary — consider intentional stamp-as-difficulty-indicator system
Acanthosis-Ann and Cherry-Angioma-Charlie could use stronger performative hooks in their power text

marketingText:
MedKayfab: DERMATOLOGY – The Surface Skirmish (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master the inflammatory rashes, the autoimmune blistering diseases, and the drug eruptions that can kill in a week.

You press a gloved thumb sideways across skin that looks like an ordinary rash, and the top layer slides off like wet wallpaper. That one sign just rewrote the patient's prognosis, and the rest of the ward is still reaching for steroid cream.

Dermatology is the one specialty where the disease sits in plain sight, which is exactly the trap. The skin is the body's border wall, the largest organ you own, and it answers every internal war the same way: red, raised, or raw. Forty conditions wear the identical angry coat. The novice sees a rash. The reader sees which siege is underway, a T-cell turbo-build, an antibody cutting the glue between two cell layers, a melanocyte going rogue and measuring its own depth in the millimetres that decide whether the patient lives.

MedKayfab Dermatology turns that border war into a narrative wrestling match, where every lesion is a character that gives itself away. Quit drilling the morphology glossary cold. Learn their faces, and the rash introduces itself the moment it steps into the ring.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (14pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- S-Tier characters like Psoriasis-Pete, Desmo the Glue, and Melanoma-Mel
- Free lifetime updates as guidelines evolve
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence, print, share, and adapt freely
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
This deck personifies the Surface layer of medicine, where the immune system, the vasculature, and the endocrine axis all leave their mark on the same wall. You meet Psoriasis-Pete, the T-cell-driven turbo-reconstruction who loves the Koebner phenomenon and shows up wherever you scratch. You meet Desmo the Glue, the desmosome holding the cell wall together until Pemphigus-Pam sends her antibody-assassins to kidnap him and the skin sloughs at a touch. Bullous-Bill takes the fight one floor down, targeting the hemidesmosomes that anchor the wall to the foundation. And looming over the whole stable is Melanoma-Mel, the most dangerous opponent in the room, whose Breslow depth quietly settles the match before anyone has called it. When SJS-Steven and TEN-Terry tag in, the skin stops being a rash and becomes an emergency.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor built for high-stress retrieval. You have the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (the morphology, the distribution, the red flags), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the diagnostic challenge). The Mechanism Flash mode is unforgiving here: if you cannot explain why the blister sits at the layer it sits in, in one sentence without looking, the patient on the Stage walks out misdiagnosed.

Honest cognitive load
This is an A-Tier deck. It rewards medical students on their dermatology rotation, anyone heading into derm, allergy, or rheumatology, and clinicians who want the visible-disease pattern bank that no textbook photo plate ever made stick. It pairs naturally with Immunology & Pathology for the hypersensitivity and autoimmune-blistering mechanisms underneath the rash, and with Internal Medicine for the systemic diseases that announce themselves on the skin before anywhere else. The drug-eruption cards shake hands with Essential Pharmacology the moment SJS-Steven names his trigger.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

PAY WHAT YOU WANT
This deck is Pay What You Want, including free. If you find it useful, a fair price is €5. If you're a student on a budget, enter €0, no questions asked. If you want to support more decks, anything above fair price is appreciated. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

DISCLAIMER
MedKayfab is a learning companion, not a clinical reference. Content was created by a physician and reviewed to the best of our knowledge, but medicine evolves, guidelines change, and some mechanisms in here will be simplified or wrong. Always verify against current primary sources and clinical guidelines before applying anything to patient care. The Blödsinn! is the vehicle. The science is serious.

Stay fluffy. — Doc FrizzleBob
